messages.subject: Barchart and Points
parts:
Dear All,
Regardless of whether it is the best visualization or not, I need to
produce something relatively simple: a barchart with some overlayed
points and a legend.
I would like some concise reusable code which I can rely upon.
So far, I somehow get the job done, but I practically double my data
set.
I paste below a self-contained example.
Any suggestion to improve my code is welcome.
Cheers

Lorenzo


###########################################
library(ggplot2)

## Initial data set I would like to plot
data_ini <- structure(list(TIME_PERIOD = c(2014, 2014, 2014, 2014,
2014,
2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014,
2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014,
2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014), OBS_VALUE =
c(15.5255319434679,
11.0013209769654, 11.1451276078035, 5.37121674230412,
5.30256399554037,
6.52821096781585, 5.50104568767542, 4.21846771621141, 4.8956374862048,
1.88943327260453, 1.79803455355281, 1.58883295207556,
1.38604439661746,
0.953758006126973, 0.707100788345785, 0.425866137002027,
18.4498212987116,
12.1122072941764, 9.94167618160538, 6.82907237956201,
6.38950437198506,
5.41425866836771, 5.27696398392558, 5.1755357032662, 4.60532125149202,
4.26905666925891, 3.31484667964721, 1.68306168169112,
1.51613971123454,
1.40250594335631, 1.2783372717054, 1.04991055559855,
0.471513654292189,
0.058947730171453), NACE_R2 = structure(c(1L, 2L, 3L, 5L, 6L,
8L, 9L, 10L, 11L, 12L, 13L, 14L, 15L, 16L, 17L, 18L, 1L, 2L,
3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 9L, 10L, 11L, 12L, 13L, 14L, 15L, 16L,
17L, 18L), .Label = c("C", "G", "L", "Q", "F", "P", "M", "O",
"K", "N", "J", "D", "S", "A", "R", "E", "B", "T"), class = "factor"),
GEO = structure(c(2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L,
2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L,
1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L), .Label = c("AT",
"EU28"
), class = "factor")), .Names = c("TIME_PERIOD",
"OBS_VALUE",
"NACE_R2", "GEO"), row.names = c("3", "7", "10", "6",
"14", "13",
"9", "12", "8", "4", "17", "1", "16", "5", "2", "18",
"31", "71",
"101", "151", "61", "141", "111", "131", "91", "121",
"81", "41",
"171", "19", "161", "51", "21", "181"), class =
"data.frame")




lbls <- levels(data_ini$GEO)

col_seq <- seq(lbls)

##I create two new data sets data1 and data2 based on data_ini.
##I will use one of them for the barchart and one for the geom_point

data1 <- data_ini
data1[data1$GEO=="EU28", ]$OBS_VALUE <- NA


data2 <- data_ini
data2[data2$GEO=="AT", ]$OBS_VALUE <- NA

gpl <- ggplot(data1, aes(x=NACE_R2, y=OBS_VALUE,
## colour=country,
fill=GEO
##
group=country
))
+

geom_bar( stat="identity",## position="dodge",
alpha=0.8
) +

geom_point(data=data2, aes(x=NACE_R2, y=OBS_VALUE,
shape=GEO),col="red",
size=5) +


theme(legend.position = 'right')+


theme(plot.title = element_text(lineheight=.8, size=24, face="bold",
vjust=1))+
theme(legend.text = element_text(vjust=1,lineheight=1 ))+
theme(legend.title = element_text(colour="black", size=16,
face="bold"))+

scale_fill_manual(NULL, breaks=lbls, labels=lbls,
values=c("blue", NA)) +

scale_shape_manual(NULL, breaks=lbls, labels= lbls,
values=c( NA, 20))


print(gpl)

Lorenzo, 

If it works for you and there are no errors, I would suggest moving forward with what you have. 

The only thing I found a bit off was that if you're plotting from two datasets as you are, it's better to leave the ggplot() call empty (AFAIK). 

I changed your filter step to use dplyr so it wouldn't wildly copy data, but otherwise it's the same. 

B

data1 <- data_ini %>% filter(GEO != "EU28")

ggplot()  +
geom_bar(data = data1, aes(x=NACE_R2, y=OBS_VALUE, fill=GEO), stat="identity", alpha=0.8) +
